claim: H1650-M3 cells are derived from H1650 cells.
source: The latter are derived from H1650 cells and harbor both phenotypic characteristics (i.e., epithelial to mesenchymal transition, increased metastatic capacity, motility, invasion and resistance to drug treatment) and molecular characteristics (i.e., increased surface expression of CD44 and decreased expression of CD24, constitutive activation of the TGF-β axis, and autocrine secretion of IL-6) of CD44+/CD24− cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) (Yao et al., 2010).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states that H1650-M3 cells are derived from H1650 cells and cites a previous publication (Yao et al., 2010).

claim: H1650-M3 cells harbor phenotypic characteristics of CD44+/CD24− cells including epithelial to mesenchymal transition, increased metastatic capacity, motility, invasion and resistance to drug treatment.
source: The latter are derived from H1650 cells and harbor both phenotypic characteristics (i.e., epithelial to mesenchymal transition, increased metastatic capacity, motility, invasion and resistance to drug treatment) and molecular characteristics (i.e., increased surface expression of CD44 and decreased expression of CD24, constitutive activation of the TGF-β axis, and autocrine secretion of IL-6) of CD44+/CD24− cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) (Yao et al., 2010).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states these phenotypic characteristics and cites a previous publication (Yao et al., 2010).

claim: H1650-M3 cells harbor molecular characteristics of CD44+/CD24− cells including increased surface expression of CD44 and decreased expression of CD24, constitutive activation of the TGF-β axis, and autocrine secretion of IL-6.
source: The latter are derived from H1650 cells and harbor both phenotypic characteristics (i.e., epithelial to mesenchymal transition, increased metastatic capacity, motility, invasion and resistance to drug treatment) and molecular characteristics (i.e., increased surface expression of CD44 and decreased expression of CD24, constitutive activation of the TGF-β axis, and autocrine secretion of IL-6) of CD44+/CD24− cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) (Yao et al., 2010).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states these molecular characteristics and cites a previous publication (Yao et al., 2010).

claim: The shRNA library used in the screen consists of 28,000 sequence-verified shRNAs designed to target approximately 9,000 genes implicated in tumorigenesis.
source: H1650 and H1650-M3 cells were infected with a retroviral shRNA library that was previously constructed in the pSM1 vector (Paddison et al., 2004). This library consists of 28,000 sequence-verified shRNAs designed to target approximately 9,000 genes that have been implicated in tumorigenesis.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes the library composition and cites the source (Paddison et al., 2004).

claim: 135 shRNAs reached a p-value of less than 0.5 and had reduced representations of more than 1-fold in H1650-M3 cells compared with H1650 cells.
source: We found that 135 shRNAs reached a p-value of less than 0.5 and had reduced representations of more than 1-fold in H1650-M3 cells compared with H1650 cells (Figure 1A).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding and references Figure 1A showing the data.

claim: shRNAs targeting IL-6 were selectively depleted in CD44+/CD24− H1650-M3 cells.
source: Among the top shRNAs selectively depleted in the CD44+/CD24− H1650-M3 cells, we identified shRNAs targeting IL-6 (Figure 1A).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding and references Figure 1A.

claim: The identification of IL-6 in the screen is consistent with previous reports indicating that the IL-6 axis is required for the survival of cells in a CD44+/CD24− state.
source: This finding is consistent with previous reports (both from our group and others) indicating that the IL-6 axis is required for the survival of cells in a CD44+/CD24− state (Yao et al., 2010; Marotta et al., 2011).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this consistency with prior literature and cites two publications (Yao et al., 2010; Marotta et al., 2011).

claim: shRNAs targeting genes in DNA repair/replication pathways such as BRCA1, ORC5L, RFC3, POLS, ERCC8 and RPA2 showed decreased representation in H1650-M3 cells.
source: Interestingly, we also observed a decreased representation of shRNA-targeted genes in DNA repair/replication pathways such as BRCA1, ORC5L, RFC3, POLS, ERCC8 and RPA2 (Figure 1A).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation and references Figure 1A.

claim: Tumor-derived cell lines with high content of CD44+/CD24− cells were more sensitive to the inactivation of IL-6, BRCA1, ORC5L, RFC3, POLS, ERCC8 and RPA2 genes.
source: Overall, we observed that tumor-derived cell lines that had a high content of CD44+/CD24− cells were more sensitive to the inactivation of these genes.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation based on validation experiments described in Figure 1B.

claim: Cancer cells grown in a uniform tissue culture in vitro microenvironment, when separated on the basis of CD44 and CD24 cell surface markers, return to their original equilibrium proportion over a relatively short period of time.
source: As shown by Gupta et al. (2011), cancer cells grown in a uniform tissue culture in vitro microenvironment, when separated on the basis of the CD44 and CD24 cell surface markers, return to their original equilibrium proportion over a relatively short period of time.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this phenomenon and cites Gupta et al. (2011).

claim: The knockdown of IL-6, BRCA1, ORC5L, RFC3, POLS, ERCC8 and RPA2 resulted in higher lethality in FACS-sorted CD44+/CD24− cells compared to cells of other immune types.
source: Overall, as illustrated in Figure 1C, we observed that the knockdown of the genes we identified in our original drop-out screen resulted in higher lethality in cells that reside in a CD44+/CD24− state compared to cells of other immune types.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation and references Figure 1C showing the data.

claim: The decrease in the number of CD44+/CD24− cells upon silencing of indicated genes was due to increased lethality in the CD44+/CD24− cell populations, not due to inter-conversion of cell states or a decrease in cell proliferation.
source: The decrease in the number of CD44+/CD24− cells was not due to inter-conversion of cell states or a decrease in cell proliferation; rather, it was the result of increased lethality in the CD44+/CD24− cell populations upon silencing of the indicated genes.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this conclusion based on multiple experimental observations.

claim: Upon inactivation of IL-6, BRCA1, ORC5L, RFC3, POLS, ERCC8 and RPA2, there was an increase in the expression of the pro-apoptotic marker Cleaved caspase-3 in H1650-M3 cells compared to parental H1650 cells.
source: In fact, upon inactivation of IL-6, BRCA1, ORC5L, RFC3, POLS, ERCC8 and RPA2, we observed (i) an increase in the expression of the pro-apoptotic marker Cleaved caspase-3 by western blot analysis in H1650-M3 cells compared to parental H1650 cells (Figure 1F, Figure 1—figure supplement 5);
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation and references Figure 1F and Figure 1—figure supplement 5.

claim: Upon inactivation of IL-6, BRCA1, ORC5L, RFC3, POLS, ERCC8 and RPA2, there was a higher number of Cleaved caspase-3 positive cells by FACS analysis in H1650 CD44+/CD24− cells compared to CD44−/CD24+ cells.
source: In fact, upon inactivation of IL-6, BRCA1, ORC5L, RFC3, POLS, ERCC8 and RPA2, we observed (i) an increase in the expression of the pro-apoptotic marker Cleaved caspase-3 by western blot analysis in H1650-M3 cells compared to parental H1650 cells (Figure 1F, Figure 1—figure supplement 5); (ii) a higher number of Cleaved caspase-3 positive cells by FACS analysis in H1650 CD44+/CD24− cells compared to CD44−/CD24+ cells (Figure 1G)
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation and references Figure 1G.

claim: Upon inactivation of IL-6, BRCA1, ORC5L, RFC3, POLS, ERCC8 and RPA2, there was a decrease in the number of colonies in the CD44+/CD24− cells in a standard clonogenic assay.
source: In fact, upon inactivation of IL-6, BRCA1, ORC5L, RFC3, POLS, ERCC8 and RPA2, we observed (i) an increase in the expression of the pro-apoptotic marker Cleaved caspase-3 by western blot analysis in H1650-M3 cells compared to parental H1650 cells (Figure 1F, Figure 1—figure supplement 5); (ii) a higher number of Cleaved caspase-3 positive cells by FACS analysis in H1650 CD44+/CD24− cells compared to CD44−/CD24+ cells (Figure 1G) and (iii) a decrease in the number of colonies in the CD44+/CD24− cells in a standard clonogenic assay (Figure 1—figure supplement 6).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation and references Figure 1—figure supplement 6.

claim: BRCA1, ORC5L, RFC3, POLS, ERCC8 and RPA2 were not mutated in any of the cell lines utilized in the study.
source: Mutation analysis of BRCA1, ORC5L, RFC3, POLS, ERCC8 and RPA2 indicated that none of these genes were mutated in any of the cell lines utilized in our study (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding and references Supplementary file 1.

claim: There were no significant differences in the levels of mRNA expression of BRCA1, ORC5L, RFC3, POLS, ERCC8 and RPA2 among the cell lines utilized.
source: Moreover, we neither observed any significant differences in the levels of their mRNA expression among the cell lines utilized (Figure 2A and B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1)
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation and references Figure 2A, 2B, and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: There were no significant variations in the efficiency of knockdown of BRCA1, ORC5L, RFC3, POLS, ERCC8 and RPA2 among the cell lines.
source: Moreover, we neither observed any significant differences in the levels of their mRNA expression among the cell lines utilized (Figure 2A and B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1) nor detected significant variations in the efficiency of their knockdown (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation and references Figure 1—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Genes known to participate in HDR and DNA damage check-point regulation, such as BLM, BRCA2, FANCF, NBN, PMS1, RAD50, RDM1, WRN, ATM and ATR, were expressed to a lesser extent in the CD44+/CD24− H1650-M3 cells than in the parental H1650 cells.
source: Yet, genes known to participate in HDR and DNA damage check-point regulation, such as BLM, BRCA2, FANCF, NBN, PMS1, RAD50, RDM1, WRN, ATM and ATR (Ciccia and Elledge, 2010), were expressed to a lesser extent in the CD44+/CD24− H1650-M3 cells than in the parental H1650 cells (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation, cites Ciccia and Elledge, 2010, and references Supplementary file 2.

claim: Cell lines with (CD44+/CD24−)hi content and FACS-sorted CD44+/CD24− cells exhibited decreased expression of BLM, BRCA2, FANCF, NBN, PMS1, RAD50, RDM1, WRN, ATM and ATR.
source: In all cases, we observed that cells lines with (CD44+/CD24−)hi content and FACS-sorted CD44+/CD24− cells exhibited decreased expression of these HDR genes.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation based on RT-qPCR analysis in multiple cell lines and primary tumors.

claim: The differential mRNA expression levels of BRCA2, RDM1 and WRN were reflected by decreased protein expression.
source: Western blot analysis of BRCA2, RDM1 and WRN also indicated that the differential mRNA expression levels we observed were reflected by decreased protein expression (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation and references Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: The combined knockdown of BRCA2 and BRCA1, RAD50 and BRCA1, or RAD50 and ORC5L resulted in a significant decrease in cell viability in A549 cells.
source: As a result, we found that the combined knockdown of BRCA2 and BRCA1, RAD50 and BRCA1, or RAD50 and ORC5L resulted in a significant decrease in cell viability, even though the individual inactivation of ORC5L, BRCA1, BRCA2 or RAD50 had no significant effect on the viability of A549 cells (Figure 2G).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding and references Figure 2G showing the data.

claim: Cells in a CD44+/CD24− state are characterized by constitutive activation of the TGF-β axis.
source: Cells in a CD44+/CD24− state are characterized by constitutive activation of the TGF-β axis that is both necessary and sufficient for the maintenance and/or acquisition of many of the features that characterize the CD44+/CD24− cell state (Figure 3A and B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1) (Mani et al., 2008).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this characteristic and cites Mani et al., 2008.

claim: TGF-β-mediated signaling is both necessary and sufficient for the maintenance and/or acquisition of many of the features that characterize the CD44+/CD24− cell state.
source: Cells in a CD44+/CD24− state are characterized by constitutive activation of the TGF-β axis that is both necessary and sufficient for the maintenance and/or acquisition of many of the features that characterize the CD44+/CD24− cell state (Figure 3A and B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1) (Mani et al., 2008).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this and cites Mani et al., 2008.

claim: TGF-β can modify the activity and expression of certain genes involved in DNA repair.
source: As previous studies have also indicated that TGF-β can modify the activity and expression of certain genes involved in DNA repair (Glick et al., 1996; Harris et al., 1997; Preobrazhenska et al., 2002; Kirshner et al., 2006; Wiegman et al., 2007), we examined whether TGF-β could be responsible for the lower expression of the HDR genes that we observed in CD44+/CD24− cells.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this and cites multiple publications (Glick et al., 1996; Harris et al., 1997; Preobrazhenska et al., 2002; Kirshner et al., 2006; Wiegman et al., 2007).

claim: Exposure to exogenous TGF-β induced the acquisition of mesenchymal-like features in cells.
source: By exposing cells to exogenous TGF-β, we confirmed that the TGF-β axis was sufficient not only to induce the acquisition of mesenchymal-like features (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A)
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation and references Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Exposure to exogenous TGF-β induced the transition into the CD44+/CD24− state.
source: By exposing cells to exogenous TGF-β, we confirmed that the TGF-β axis was sufficient not only to induce the acquisition of mesenchymal-like features (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A) and the transition into the CD44+/CD24− state (Figure 3C)
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation and references Figure 3C.

claim: Exposure to exogenous TGF-β decreased the expression of BLM, BRCA2, FANCF, NBN, PMS1, RAD50, RDM1, WRN, ATM and ATR in multiple tumor-derived cell lines.
source: By exposing cells to exogenous TGF-β, we confirmed that the TGF-β axis was sufficient not only to induce the acquisition of mesenchymal-like features (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A) and the transition into the CD44+/CD24− state (Figure 3C) but also to decrease the expression of BLM, BRCA2, FANCF, NBN, PMS1, RAD50, RDM1, WRN, ATM and ATR in multiple tumor-derived cell lines (Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation and references Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 2B.

claim: TGF-β induced a decrease in protein expression of BRCA2, BLM and RAD50.
source: In the case of BRCA2, BLM and RAD50, we confirmed that TGF-β also induced a decrease in protein expression as assessed through western blot analyses of cell extracts (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation and references Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: Treatment of CD44+/CD24− H1650-M3 cells with selective inhibitors of TGFBRI (LY2157299 and LY364947) augmented the expression of ATR, BLM, BRCA2, FANCF, NBN, PMS1 and RAD50.
source: Conversely, treatment of the CD44+/CD24− H1650-M3 cells with two selective inhibitors of TGFBRI (LY2157299 and LY364947) augmented the expression of ATR, BLM, BRCA2, FANCF, NBN, PMS1 and RAD50 and, as expected, decreased the expression of the TGF-β-induced genes SERPINE1, SNAIL, SKIL and ZEB1 (Figure 3E and Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation and references Figure 3E and Figure 3—figure supplement 4.

claim: Treatment of CD44+/CD24− H1650-M3 cells with selective inhibitors of TGFBRI (LY2157299 and LY364947) decreased the expression of the TGF-β-induced genes SERPINE1, SNAIL, SKIL and ZEB1.
source: Conversely, treatment of the CD44+/CD24− H1650-M3 cells with two selective inhibitors of TGFBRI (LY2157299 and LY364947) augmented the expression of ATR, BLM, BRCA2, FANCF, NBN, PMS1 and RAD50 and, as expected, decreased the expression of the TGF-β-induced genes SERPINE1, SNAIL, SKIL and ZEB1 (Figure 3E and Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation and references Figure 3E and Figure 3—figure supplement 4.

claim: TGF-β-mediated signaling is sufficient and necessary to decrease the expression of the HDR genes that were observed to be downregulated in CD44+/CD24− cells.
source: Altogether, these data indicate that TGF-β-mediated signaling is sufficient and necessary to decrease the expression of the HDR genes that we observed to be downregulated in CD44+/CD24− cells.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this conclusion based on the experimental data presented.

claim: In human breast tumor dataset (BRCA) generated by the TCGA Research Network, both TGFB1 and the TGF-β signature genes were inversely correlated with the expression of BLM, BRCA2, FANCF, NBN, PMS1, RAD50, RDM1, WRN, ATM and ATR.
source: We found that, consistent with our previous observations, both TGFB1 and the TGF-β signature genes were inversely correlated with the expression of BLM, BRCA2, FANCF, NBN, PMS1, RAD50, RDM1, WRN, ATM and ATR (Figure 3F).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding from TCGA data analysis and references Figure 3F.

claim: In H1650 and U2OS cells, TGF-β did not induce any significant changes in the distribution of cells in G1/S/G2 within 9 hours.
source: Yet, in H1650 and U2OS cells, although TGF-β reduced the expression of DNA repair genes within 9 hr (Figure 3D), it did not induce any significant changes in the distribution of cells in G1/S/G2 within the same timeframe (Figure 3—figure supplement 5).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation and references Figure 3—figure supplement 5.

claim: CD44+/CD24− cells had a higher number of γ-H2AX positive foci compared to CD44−/CD24+ cells.
source: We found that CD44+/CD24− cells had a higher number of γ-H2AX positive foci (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation and references Figure 4A and B.

claim: H1650-M3 cells had a higher number of DSBs compared with H1650 cells as confirmed by comet assay.
source: The larger mean comet-tail movement in H1650-M3 cells compared with H1650 cells confirmed a higher number of DSBs in CD44+/CD24− cells (Figure 4F and G).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation and references Figure 4F and G.

claim: TGF-β treatment was sufficient to increase the number of 53BP1/γ-H2AX double-positive foci in A549, H1650 and MCF7 cells.
source: Also in this case, we found that TGF-β treatment was sufficient to increase the number of 53BP1/γ-H2AX double-positive foci and the mean comet tail movement (Figure 4C, D, F and G and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation and references Figure 4C, D, F, G and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: TGF-β treatment was sufficient to increase the mean comet tail movement in A549, H1650 and MCF7 cells.
source: Also in this case, we found that TGF-β treatment was sufficient to increase the number of 53BP1/γ-H2AX double-positive foci and the mean comet tail movement (Figure 4C, D, F and G and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation and references Figure 4C, D, F, G and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Upon transfection with pCBASce-I, there was a significant reduction in GFP-positive cells among U2OS cells and H1650 cells treated with TGF-β.
source: By using this assay, upon transfection with pCBASce-I, we observed a significant reduction in GFP-positive cells among U2OS cells as well as among H1650 cells treated with TGF-β (Figure 4I and Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation and references Figure 4I and Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: CD44+/CD24− cells from three human NSCLC tumors and a tumor-derived cell line possessed a higher content of DNA joint points compared to CD44−/CD24+ cells.
source: Whole-genome CNA analysis in FACS-sorted CD44+/CD24− and CD44−/CD24+ cells from three human NSCLC tumors and a tumor-derived cell line showed that the CD44+/CD24− cells possessed a higher content of DNA joint points and the distinctive saw-tooth profile (Kwei et al., 2010) (Figure 5A, B, C and F and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation, cites Kwei et al., 2010, and references multiple figures.

claim: CD44+/CD24− cells from three human NSCLC tumors and a tumor-derived cell line possessed the distinctive saw-tooth profile.
source: Whole-genome CNA analysis in FACS-sorted CD44+/CD24− and CD44−/CD24+ cells from three human NSCLC tumors and a tumor-derived cell line showed that the CD44+/CD24− cells possessed a higher content of DNA joint points and the distinctive saw-tooth profile (Kwei et al., 2010) (Figure 5A, B, C and F and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation, cites Kwei et al., 2010, and references multiple figures.

claim: The increased DNA joint points and saw-tooth profile in CD44+/CD24− cells was due to an intrinsic property of CD44+/CD24− cells, not to concealed genetic mutations or expansion of a single clonal population with high DNA DSBs.
source: In addition, CNA analysis of a H1650 isogenic cell line (H1650-Isg-E4) also established that this was due neither to concealed genetic mutations (Figure 5D, E and F and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B) nor to the expansion of a single clonal population with high DNA DSBs (Figure 5G and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B), but rather to an intrinsic property of CD44+/CD24− cells.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this conclusion based on analysis of isogenic cell lines and references multiple figures.

claim: The decreased expression of HDR genes and a reduced DNA repair proficiency could result in a hyper-mutable phenotype and an increased genetic diversity of CD44+/CD24− cells.
source: On the basis of these observations, we concluded that the decreased expression of HDR genes and a reduced DNA repair proficiency could result in a hyper-mutable phenotype and an increased genetic diversity of CD44+/CD24− cells.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this conclusion based on the experimental observations.

claim: TGF-β treatment was sufficient to increase the number of DNA joint points in H1650-Isg-D6 cells.
source: Much like our observations in CD44+/CD24− cells, we detected an overall expansion in the number of DNA joint points and an increased genetic heterogeneity of H1650-Isg-D6 cells upon exposure to TGF-β (Figure 6A, B and C).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation and references Figure 6A, B and C.

claim: TGF-β treatment was sufficient to increase the genetic heterogeneity of H1650-Isg-D6 cells.
source: Much like our observations in CD44+/CD24− cells, we detected an overall expansion in the number of DNA joint points and an increased genetic heterogeneity of H1650-Isg-D6 cells upon exposure to TGF-β (Figure 6A, B and C).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation and references Figure 6A, B and C.

claim: When treated with TGF-β, A549 cells transit into a CD44+/CD24− state.
source: We took advantage of the fact that when treated with TGF-β, A549 cells transit into a CD44+/CD24− state (i.e., differential surface expression of CD44 and CD24, increased expression of VIM, SNAI1 and IL-6 and decreased expression of both E-cadherin (CDH1) and the HDR genes described previously), but upon TGF-β withdrawal, they return to their original epithelial state (Figure 7A and Band Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation and references Figure 7A, B and Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: Upon TGF-β withdrawal, A549 cells return to their original epithelial state.
source: We took advantage of the fact that when treated with TGF-β, A549 cells transit into a CD44+/CD24− state (i.e., differential surface expression of CD44 and CD24, increased expression of VIM, SNAI1 and IL-6 and decreased expression of both E-cadherin (CDH1) and the HDR genes described previously), but upon TGF-β withdrawal, they return to their original epithelial state (Figure 7A and Band Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation and references Figure 7A, B and Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: Transient exposure to TGF-β results in an increased genetic diversity in A549 cells.
source: We found that transient exposure to TGF-β results in an increased genetic diversity (Figure 7C).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding and references Figure 7C.

claim: A549 TGF-β-naïve cells and A549 cells that were transiently exposed to TGF-β for 3 weeks and 6 weeks (A549-3w△ and A549-6w△, respectively) had similar half maximal inhibitory concentrations (IC50s) when treated with different concentrations of epitaxol, cisplatin, doxorubicin, erlotinib and tunicamycin.
source: When we treated A549 TGF-β-naïve cells and A549 cells that were transiently exposed to TGF-β for 3 weeks and 6 weeks (A549-3w△ and A549-6w△, respectively) with different concentrations of epitaxol, cisplatin, doxorubicin, erlotinib and tunicamycin, we found that they had similar half maximal inhibitory concentrations (IC50s) (Figure 7D)
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation and references Figure 7D.

claim: When cells were treated with very high concentrations of tunicamycin, epitaxol and cisplatin, the number of colonies that could survive the drug treatment was consistently and significantly higher for A549-3w△ and A549-6w△ cells compared to A549 TGF-β-naïve cells.
source: This was not the case when cells were treated with very high concentrations of tunicamycin, epitaxol and cisplatin. In this experiment, the number of colonies that could survive the drug treatment was in fact consistently and significantly higher for A549-3w△ and A549-6w△ cells (Figure 7E).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation and references Figure 7E.

claim: Tunicamycin-resistant clones retained resistance to tunicamycin but were still sensitive to taxol.
source: But when we tested the sensitivity of tunicamycin-resistant clones to tunicamycin and taxol, we observed that these cells retained resistance to tunicamycin but were still sensitive to taxol. This result indicated that any particular clonal population was not selected but rather presented the possibility that their resistance was due to diverse molecular mechanisms (Figure 7F).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation and references Figure 7F.

claim: CD44+/CD24− cancer cells are genetically highly unstable because of intrinsic defects in their DNA-repair capabilities.
source: Here, we report that human CD44+/CD24− cancer cells are genetically highly unstable because of intrinsic defects in their DNA-repair capabilities.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this as a main finding in the abstract.

claim: In CD44+/CD24− cells, constitutive activation of the TGF-beta axis was both necessary and sufficient to reduce the expression of genes that are crucial in coordinating DNA damage repair mechanisms.
source: In fact, in CD44+/CD24− cells, constitutive activation of the TGF-beta axis was both necessary and sufficient to reduce the expression of genes that are crucial in coordinating DNA damage repair mechanisms.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this as a main finding in the abstract.

claim: Cancer cells that reside in a CD44+/CD24− state are characterized by increased accumulation of DNA copy number alterations.
source: Consequently, we observed that cancer cells that reside in a CD44+/CD24− state are characterized by increased accumulation of DNA copy number alterations, greater genetic diversity and improved adaptability to drug treatment.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this as a main finding in the abstract.

claim: Cancer cells that reside in a CD44+/CD24− state are characterized by greater genetic diversity.
source: Consequently, we observed that cancer cells that reside in a CD44+/CD24− state are characterized by increased accumulation of DNA copy number alterations, greater genetic diversity and improved adaptability to drug treatment.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this as a main finding in the abstract.

claim: Cancer cells that reside in a CD44+/CD24− state are characterized by improved adaptability to drug treatment.
source: Consequently, we observed that cancer cells that reside in a CD44+/CD24− state are characterized by increased accumulation of DNA copy number alterations, greater genetic diversity and improved adaptability to drug treatment.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this as a main finding in the abstract.

claim: The transition into a CD44+/CD24− cell state can promote intra-tumor genetic heterogeneity, spur tumor evolution and increase tumor fitness.
source: Together, these data suggest that the transition into a CD44+/CD24− cell state can promote intra-tumor genetic heterogeneity, spur tumor evolution and increase tumor fitness.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this conclusion in the abstract.

claim: CD44+/CD24− cancer cells are more adept at forming tumors.
source: It has been shown that CD44+/CD24− cancer cells are more adept at forming tumors, are more resistant to chemotherapy and tend to have greater metastatic potential (Al-Hajj et al., 2003; Polyak and Weinberg, 2009; Yao et al., 2010; Korkaya et al., 2011; Brooks et al., 2015).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this and cites multiple publications.

claim: CD44+/CD24− cancer cells are more resistant to chemotherapy.
source: It has been shown that CD44+/CD24− cancer cells are more adept at forming tumors, are more resistant to chemotherapy and tend to have greater metastatic potential (Al-Hajj et al., 2003; Polyak and Weinberg, 2009; Yao et al., 2010; Korkaya et al., 2011; Brooks et al., 2015).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this and cites multiple publications.

claim: CD44+/CD24− cancer cells tend to have greater metastatic potential.
source: It has been shown that CD44+/CD24− cancer cells are more adept at forming tumors, are more resistant to chemotherapy and tend to have greater metastatic potential (Al-Hajj et al., 2003; Polyak and Weinberg, 2009; Yao et al., 2010; Korkaya et al., 2011; Brooks et al., 2015).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this and cites multiple publications.

claim: CD44+/CD24− cells were initially identified in breast tumors and breast-cancer-derived cell lines.
source: CD44+/CD24− cells were initially identified in breast tumors and breast-cancer-derived cell lines and have since been observed in the vast majority of tumors and tumor-derived cell lines, including non-small-cell lung carcinomas (NSCLCs), glioblastomas, neuroblastomas and leiomyosarcomas, as well as pancreatic, colon, prostate and ovarian tumors/cancers.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this.

claim: CD44+/CD24− cells have been observed in the vast majority of tumors and tumor-derived cell lines, including non-small-cell lung carcinomas (NSCLCs), glioblastomas, neuroblastomas and leiomyosarcomas, as well as pancreatic, colon, prostate and ovarian tumors/cancers.
source: CD44+/CD24− cells were initially identified in breast tumors and breast-cancer-derived cell lines and have since been observed in the vast majority of tumors and tumor-derived cell lines, including non-small-cell lung carcinomas (NSCLCs), glioblastomas, neuroblastomas and leiomyosarcomas, as well as pancreatic, colon, prostate and ovarian tumors/cancers.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this.
